general_information.Description: -Objective: Help students develop clear and intelligible English pronunciation with a neutral and comprehensible accent. Help students recognize and produce individual English consonant sounds, including place of articulation, manner of articulation, voicing contrasts, aspiration, difficult contrasts (/θ/–/s/, /ʃ/–/s/, /r/–/l/…) (e.g., /θ/–/s/, /ʃ/–/s/, /r/–/l/) Help students identify diversity of sound systems. Help students know how to use AI-assisted tools to practice pronunciation tools (e.g., ELSA, SpeechAce, Speechling) to receive instant feedback, identify mispronounced sounds, and improve segmental features. Help students know how to recognize and produce correct word stress, sentence stress, weak forms, linking, and rhythm. Help students know how to practice shadowing with AI-generated audio to improve naturalness and speech fluency. Help students know how to distinguish segmental features Help students know how to diagnose personal listening weaknesses through AI performance analytics. Help students know how to develop self-learning habits using AI apps for daily pronunciation practice. '-Description: 'This course covers key features of English pronunciation, including consonants, vowels, diphthongs, sound combinations, word and sentence stress, rhythm, intonation, tone, accents, and phonemic symbols. Students develop clearer and more fluent speech through practical exercises and AI-supported pronunciation practice. '-Teaching method: optional '- Apply AI tools effectively to support self-study, self-practice.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination '- Actively participate in class activities '- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class '- Use their own laptops and headphones in class only for learning purposes '- Use AI tools effectively and responsibly '- Read the textbook in advance
general_information.Tools: 1. AI Tools for pronunciation practice & phonetic transcription - ChatGPT – giải thích quy tắc IPA, tạo bảng âm, sửa lỗi phát âm - YouGlish (AI-indexed examples) – nghe mẫu phát âm thật theo ngữ cảnh - Elsa Speak / Speechling – luyện phát âm với phản hồi AI - IPA Transcriber AI – tự động chuyển văn bản sang phiên âm IPA - Praat + AI-assisted plugins – phân tích sóng âm, formant, pitch 2. AI Tools for creating interactive exercises - ChatGPT – tạo bài tập nhận diện âm, minimal pairs, stress patterns - Twee – tạo bài trắc nghiệm minimal pairs, word stress - Quizizz AI – tạo quiz nghe–chọn âm, phân biệt âm dễ nhầm - Edpuzzle AI – tạo bài nghe dựa trên video phát â - Genially AI – làm bài tập kéo–thả IPA hoặc matching 3. AI Tools for visualizing speech sounds & articulation - VocalImage / AnatomyNext – mô phỏng 3D articulators - Wakaru / SoundLab AI – hình ảnh hóa sóng âm, formant, spectrogram - Canva AI – tạo infographic về vowel chart / consonant chart - Descript – tạo audio waveform và chỉnh sửa giọng bằng AI

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Recognize and accurately produce consonant sounds of English, and differentiate them clearly in both spoken and written (IPA) forms, with support from AI pronunciation feedback tools.
Recognize and accurately produce vowel sounds of English, and distinguish vowel contrasts through listening and transcription tasks supported by AI analysis.
Recognize and accurately produce diphthongs and triphthongs of English, and demonstrate clear differences between similar complex vowels using AI-assisted pronunciation practice.
Demonstrate fluency and appropriate prosody—intonation patterns, sentence stress—to express different meanings and emotions in spoken English, using AI models for practice and comparison.
Apply rules of connected speech (linking, assimilation, elision, weak forms) to produce smoother and more natural speech, with reinforcement from AI-based listening and speaking tools.

Collaborate effectively in pairs and groups to practice pronunciation, solve phonetic/phonological tasks, provide peer feedback, and engage in sustained pronunciation improvement supported by AI-enhanced learning resources.

assessments.Question Type: Teachers can flexibly choose different formats for students to complete the assignment. Here are some suggestions for teachers to choose:Suggestion 1: Students record speakers who have mispronunciations (they can be students from outside the class or students within the class) and use those recordings as the main material for creating the pronunciation guide. Those short clips should only be used as practice examples or for comparison with the mispronounced samples. The content should focus only on analyzing consonant and vowel sounds.Students analyze the clip focusing only on the content they have learned:A. Consonant Sounds· Identify and list examples of consonants in the clip that are commonly difficult for Vietnamese learners (e.g., /θ/, /ð/, /ʃ/, /tʃ/, /ʒ/, /v/, /z/, final stops /p t k/, etc.).· Provide short IPA transcriptions only for word-level items, not full sentences.· Identify misleading spellings (e.g., “knife” /naɪf/)B. Vowel Sounds· Identify key vowel sounds in the clip that differ significantly from Vietnamese vowels.· Provide minimal IPA transcription of sample words (e.g., ship vs sheep, cup vs calf).· Comment briefly on vowel length contrasts or tense vs. lax vowel differences, if applicable.No analysis of diphthongs, triphthongs, stress, linking, rhythm, or intonation.Group Collaboration:Work in teams of 3–4 to compile findings and present them in a short video or slide presentation.Suggestion 2:Students work in pairs and make a dialogue in which they should use the following aspects of sounds (the same as Speaking part 1 in FE)- Vowels- Consonants- Dipthongs- Elision- Linking consonant sounds to vowel sounds- Intrusion- Assimilation

assessments.Question Type: Oral exam – In pairs and in person. Part 1: Each student performs a pronunciation and analysis task based on a prepared script. (Individual) Part 2: Students perform a role-play simulating a real-life conversation. (Pair)
assessments.No Question: 2 - Part 1: One script (150 words) to read aloud per student + One individual analysis task. Part 2: One role-play per pair.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Test students' ability to apply the knowledge which student obtained in the delivered units.
assessments.Grading Guide: Exam room Structure Face-to-face oral exam 2 parts: Part 1 – Individual Task (7 minutes per student, including 2 minutes for preparation) Part 2 – Pair Task (7 minutes per pair, including 3 minutes for preparation) Pairing Students are paired randomly before the exam. If the number is odd → examiner can call a volunteer to step in as a partner. Timing Part 1 (Individual): 7 minutes per student. Part 2 (Pair): 7 minutes per pair. Total: ~20 minutes for a whole part Equipment Cue cards (printed passages and role-play scenarios). Timer/stopwatch (examiner's device) Exam Sets Part 1 – Individual Task (Reading + Analysis): prepare 10 short passages (~150 words, same difficulty). Part 2 – Pair Task (Role-play): prepare 6–8 role-play situations (e.g., complimenting, job interview, ordering food, customer service, travel inquiry, weekend planning, etc.). Retake Policy: Student will be marked personally => If only one student in the course fails, the retake will be done as a pair with the examiner.
